notes: No release before 0.5.0 may claim any of this is balanced: every magnitude in the shipped content carries tuningStatus untuned and the balance harness owns all of them -- so this file is a measurement and not a balance claim.

The universe is still degenerate in the following ways, and this edit closes two of them and withdraws two statements the superseded files made. The fast and horizon sweeps are 100 percent passive-control and submit no god verb; the ascension sweep round-robins all eight strategies, which is the one place a strategy is exercised at all, and the superseded files called all three passive. Scribing no longer stops for good when the stock empties: the single materials pool is now food, stone and vellum and a scribe spends only vellum, so over the reference two hundred years the final twenty-year window scribes 5 books where it used to scribe none. Portals now open. The superseded files say nothing in packages/scenario opens one and that no raid runs in any committed sweep, and that is no longer true: raids.ts installs the arrival process and drives rules-raid to termination, and the executor declares raidEngagement true by default. Teaching does not die out either -- but the superseded files' statement that a lesson is taught in every one of the ten twenty-year windows, the thinnest holding 16, is withdrawn as false. It held for one run seed. Three of five seeds violate it on the tree those files were measured on, and three of five violate it here. Teaching supply oscillates and a two-hundred-year horizon can end inside a trough; packages/scenario/test/unit/reference-long-run.test.ts carries the seeds, the per-window supply counts and the three explanations they rule out.
rationale: The economy wire arriving in the gate sweeps, regenerated once from the merged tree. The merge took main's three baselines as an explicit placeholder rather than hand-merging this branch's against them, so every delta recorded here is this tree against main at f97cc76 -- a comparison somebody can reproduce -- and not against an intermediate nobody ran. The content set changed and the digest says so, 6b18886a -> ba7be8d6: fourteen form.json records gained yieldWeights, five territory.json records gained yieldPerLandUnit, seven raid constants that make a raid fire were added, and main's max-summons-per-side edit from 16 to 8 came across. Two things changed at once and the split between them is not measured here: the economy wire, and raids firing in a committed sweep for the first time -- main's executor declares raidEngagement false because nothing there opens a portal, and this tree's declares it true. Attributing the movements below to one or the other wants the A/B the executor already carries, a run built with raids false, and that is a measurement rather than a merge. No tolerance was widened, and no constant, cap or magnitude was tuned to produce any movement below. At twenty world years the split has had time to bite and referenceGrimoires carries the largest movement in any of the three files: 353.605 -> 321.5 (-32.105, -4.23 SE), a ninth of the books. referenceKnowledgeInstances follows it down, 1025.03 -> 1003.91 (-21.12, -2.44 SE), and referenceLibraryDepth with it, 19.045 -> 18.64 (-0.405, -0.55 SE). The finding worth reading is what did not move: referenceNodesKnown (41.845) and referenceNodesGained (39.345) are identical to the digit, 0.00 SE. The vellum split costs this universe books, not knowledge -- what a mage knows is unchanged and what is written down is not. The rest is small: referencePeakPopulation 360 -> 353 (-7, -1.41 SE), referencePopulation and referencePopulationChange each up 0.53 (0.42 SE), referenceNodesGainedFinalQuarter 7.595 -> 7.645 (0.05, 0.46 SE), referenceLivingMages up 0.02 (0.10 SE).
